author: @TobeyIkeh
text:
Ngl, as a bassist and sometimes guitarist, I can speak for a lot of musicians when I say, almost nobody likes these electronic instruments. Electronic drum kits are actually cool because they are very convenient given the nature of drums. Electronic pianos work really well, very convenient and replicate the sound nearly if not spot on, synths have their place, and electronic wind instruments are great for practice. I get it, they (electronic guitars) are for fun and not for serious musicians, but honestly, even if you are playing instruments for casual fun, you will legitimately feel more gratified and satisfied learning the actual instrument. Musical instruments are things that will probably never change, or at least barely will, in their basic functionality. A lot of them haven't even changed much from the past.

Edit: I'm talking specifically about the electronic guitar. I've already made the adjustment in my earlier statement. A lot of electronic instruments are cool and genuinely worth it because of the convenience they have and that they produce the real sounds while still maintaining a lot of original functionally. 

My issue is that the electronic guitar is made and marketed to be something that it is really not, and cost wise in a lot of cases, is genuinely not even worth it, even as a gimmick. Why would I justify spending money getting a digital guitar that has piano sounds, if I can just get a digital piano lol, even for cheap. I wish these type of guitars aren't marketed as alternatives because they might look like guitars but functionally, they are not. It's only worth it if you genuinely do not have the time to learn a real thing or you don't see yourself advancing musically
